mainTopic: Paying a קנס (fine) for slaughtering a stolen animal when the act also carries the death penalty: רבה's rulings on שבת and מחתרת, and רב פפא's case of a cow.
overview: The גמרא explains that רבי מאיר accepts 'flogged and pays' but not 'dies and pays.' A קנס is different, though, because the Torah made a special rule that a fine is paid even by someone liable to death. רבה follows this idea. A thief who stole an animal earlier and then slaughters it on שבת, or during a break-in (מחתרת), still pays the fine. If the stealing and the capital act happen together, he is exempt from everything. The גמרא shows why רבה needed to teach both cases. רב פפא then teaches that a borrowed cow slaughtered on שבת brings no payment, because a borrower's liability for accidents begins only when the accident happens. רבא rules on heirs who inherit a borrowed cow, and the גמרא gives two versions of his ruling, one that agrees with רב פפא and one that does not. Finally the גמרא returns to the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about an unwarned sinner who deserves death or lashes and also owes money. ריש לקיש begins a challenge from a פסוק, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's view: flogged and pays, but not dies and pays
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that רבי מאיר holds a person can be flogged and also pay, but cannot be executed and also pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר holds that someone can be flogged and still pay, but he does not hold that someone can be put to death and still pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is clarifying exactly what רבי מאיר holds about getting a punishment and paying money for the same act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when one act brings both a punishment and a payment, only the bigger punishment is given. רבי מאיר makes an exception for flogging, so the person is flogged and also pays. For the death penalty he agrees with the usual rule, so there is no payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Is flogged and also pays money
Is put to death and also pays money
He holds this view / he does not hold this view

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, לוֹקֶה וּמְשַׁלֵּם אִית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir holds that one is flogged and pays,
but he does not hold that one dies and pays.
phrases.notes: 'Dies' here means he is put to death by בית דין for the same act.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, לוֹקֶה וּמְשַׁלֵּם אִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about רבי מאיר's position.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the exact limits of רבי מאיר's view
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר requires payment together with flogging, but not together with the death penalty.

steps.title: Fines are a special Torah exception
steps.stepSummary: A קנס is different: the Torah made a new rule that a fine is paid even when the person is executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: These cases are different, because the Torah made a special new rule about fines: even though he is put to death, he still pays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a fine is still paid even though רבי מאיר normally holds that a person who is executed does not pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is not ordinary payment for damage. It is a penalty the Torah created. Since the whole idea is a חידוש, the usual rule that the bigger punishment cancels the payment does not apply. So the thief pays the fine even if he is liable to death.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
A new rule that goes against normal logic
A fine; a penalty payment beyond the actual loss
He is killed (executed)

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the base for all of רבה's rulings that come next.

phrases.english: And these cases are different,
for it is a novelty that the Torah introduced regarding a fine:
even though he is killed, he pays.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁאנֵי הָנֵי, דְּחִידּוּשׁ הוּא שֶׁחִידְּשָׁה תּוֹרָה בִּקְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 1. The rule 'no dies and pays' does not apply to fines.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי מאיר holds 'no dies and pays,' someone liable to death would not pay a fine.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קנס is a Torah novelty and is paid even when the person is liable to death.

steps.title: רבה's ruling: a stolen kid slaughtered on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that if the theft came before שבת, the slaughter fine is paid. If the theft and the slaughter on שבת happened together, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה is consistent with his view, for רבה said: If a person already had a stolen young goat and slaughtered it on שבת, he must pay, because he became liable for the theft before he broke שבת. If he stole it and slaughtered it on שבת, he is exempt, because without liability for the theft there is no liability for slaughtering or selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבה holds the same idea, that a fine is paid even with the death penalty, in another ruling of his about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the theft happened earlier, the theft liability is already in place. The slaughter fine is a קנס, so it is paid even though slaughtering on שבת carries the death penalty. When the theft itself happens together with the שבת violation, the death penalty cancels the theft liability. The slaughter fine depends on the theft, so it falls away too.

keyTerms.meaning: Follows his own reasoning, consistent with what he said elsewhere
A young goat
Slaughtering, which brings the four-or-five payment for a thief
Selling the stolen animal, which also brings the four-or-five payment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. 'היה גדי גנוב לו' means he stole it before, so he is liable. 'גנב וטבח בשבת' means the stealing happened together with the שבת act, so he is exempt.

phrases.english: And Rabba follows his own reasoning,
for Rabba said:
If he had a stolen kid,
and he slaughtered it on Shabbat, he is liable,
since he had already become liable for the theft
before he came to the prohibition of Shabbat.
If he stole and slaughtered on Shabbat, he is exempt,
for if there is no theft,
there is no slaughter and there is no sale.
phrases.notes: The fine for slaughtering or selling only exists on top of liability for the theft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבה applying the principle from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a קנס is paid even when the act carries the death penalty
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's own ruling about a stolen kid slaughtered on שבת

steps.title: רבה's ruling: a stolen kid slaughtered during a burglary
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives the same two-part ruling for a burglar breaking in, who is treated like someone liable to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: If a person already had a stolen young goat and slaughtered it while breaking in, he must pay, because he became liable for the theft before he came to the prohibition of breaking in. If he stole it and slaughtered it while breaking in, he is exempt, because without liability for the theft there is no liability for slaughtering or selling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה repeats the same rule, but this time with a burglar breaking in through a tunnel (מחתרת) instead of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A burglar breaking in can be killed by the homeowner, so he has the status of someone liable for his life. If the theft came earlier, the slaughter fine is still paid, since it is a קנס. If the theft happened during the break-in, the theft liability falls away, and so does the fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking in by tunneling; a burglar caught this way may be killed
Exempt
Liable

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
If he had a stolen kid
and he slaughtered it during a break-in, he is liable,
since he had already become liable for the theft
before he came to the prohibition of breaking in.
If he stole and slaughtered during a break-in, he is exempt,
for if there is no theft,
there is no slaughter and there is no sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה: הָיָה גְּדִי גָּנוּב לוֹ וּטְבָחוֹ בַּמַּחְתֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling by רבה that applies the same logic to מחתרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earlier theft followed by slaughter during a break-in means he pays the fine. Theft and slaughter together during a break-in means he is exempt.

steps.title: Why רבה needed to teach both cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that each case has its own special strength, so we could not learn one from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both cases are needed. If he had taught only שבת, we would say that is because its prohibition is permanent, but burglary is only a temporary prohibition, so maybe not. If he had taught only burglary, we would say that is because breaking in counts as his warning, but שבת needs a warning, so maybe not. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why did רבה say the same rule twice? It shows that each case teaches something the other could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת is stronger because the death penalty for it always applies, while the burglar is only killable at the moment of the break-in. Burglary is stronger because no warning is needed, while שבת requires התראה before there is a death penalty. Since each case is stronger in a different way, neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary, so both statements are needed
A permanent prohibition that always applies
A temporary prohibition, only for the moment
A warning given before the sin, needed for בית דין to punish
I would say not, so the rule might not apply

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule, that a קנס is paid even with a death-penalty act if the theft came first, applies both to שבת and to מחתרת. Each case needed to be stated.

phrases.english: And it is necessary.
For if he had taught us only Shabbat,
that would be because its prohibition is a permanent prohibition.
But a break-in, which is a temporary prohibition,
I would say not.
And if he had taught us only a break-in,
that would be because his breaking in is his warning.
phrases.notes: Breaking in itself shows what he is ready to do, so no spoken warning is needed.

phrases.english: But Shabbat, which requires a warning,
I would say not. So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why steps 3 and 4 are not repetitive.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each case is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One of רבה's statements seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case has its own strength, so both had to be taught.

steps.title: רב פפא: a stolen cow versus a borrowed cow slaughtered on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that a cow stolen earlier and slaughtered on שבת brings liability, but a borrowed cow slaughtered on שבת brings exemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If a person had a stolen cow and slaughtered it on שבת, he is liable, because he became liable for the theft before he broke שבת. If a cow was lent to him and he slaughtered it on שבת, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא states his own ruling, using a cow, and adds the case of a borrowed animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stolen cow works like רבה's kid, since the theft came first. With a borrowed cow, the borrower's duty to pay for its loss only starts when the loss happens, which here is the slaughter. That is the same moment he breaks שבת, so the death penalty cancels the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: A cow
Borrowed (lent to him)
Stolen

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If he had a stolen cow,
and he slaughtered it on Shabbat, he is liable,
since he had already become liable for the theft
before he came to the prohibition of Shabbat.
If a cow was lent to him,
and he slaughtered it on Shabbat, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: His duty to pay for the cow starts only when he slaughters it, and that is the same moment he breaks שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָיְתָה פָּרָה גְּנוּבָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement that looks very similar to רבה's ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stolen earlier and slaughtered on שבת means he is liable. Borrowed and slaughtered on שבת means he is exempt.

steps.title: What did רב פפא add?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי whether רב פפא only came to teach that the rule applies to a cow, which seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, said to רב אשי: Did רב פפא come just to teach us about a cow?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges רב פפא's statement, because it seems to repeat what רבה already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה already taught the rule with a kid. Switching to a cow should not change anything. So the question is what new point רב פפא was trying to make.

keyTerms.meaning: He came to teach us
The son of

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
Did Rav Pappa come to teach us about a cow?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 6 as seemingly redundant next to step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's statement about the stolen cow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה already taught the same rule with a kid, and the type of animal makes no difference, so רב פפא's statement seems to add nothing.

steps.title: רב פפא's real point is the borrowed cow
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that רב פפא's new teaching is about the borrowed cow. We might have thought a borrower is liable for accidents from the moment he borrows it, so slaughtering it on שבת would still bring liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב פפא came to teach us about a borrowed cow. You might have thought that since רב פפא said a borrower must feed the animal from the moment he pulls it into his possession, he is also liable for its accidents from the moment he borrows it. So רב פפא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from step 7. רב פפא was not teaching something obvious about a cow; his חידוש is the borrowed cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a reason to think the borrower is liable from the start, because רב פפא himself said he must feed the animal from the moment of pulling it. If so, liability for accidents might also start right away, before שבת, and then the שבת slaughter would not exempt him. רב פפא teaches that liability for accidents begins only when the accident happens, so if that moment is on שבת, he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Borrowed (a borrowed animal)
It could have entered your mind to say (this introduces the mistaken first thought)
Pulling the animal into one's possession, a way of taking ownership or responsibility
Its unavoidable accidents, which a borrower must normally pay for
He teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a borrower's liability for accidents begins when the accident happens, not when he borrows. This idea is tested again in the next steps.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי answering רב אחא בריה דרבא's question from the last step.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa came to teach us about a borrowed cow.
It could have entered your mind to say,
since Rav Pappa said:
It is from the moment of pulling it
that he becomes obligated to feed it,
so here too:
from the moment of borrowing he is liable for its accidents.
So he teaches us that this is not so.
phrases.notes: The borrower becomes liable only when the accident happens, which here is the slaughter on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַב פָּפָּא, שְׁאוּלָה אֲתָא לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the real חידוש: the focus is the borrowed-cow case, not the cow itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a borrower must feed the animal from the moment of pulling, he would be liable for accidents from the moment of borrowing, so the שבת slaughter would not exempt him
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability for accidents begins only when the accident happens; if that is on שבת, he is exempt

steps.title: Children who inherit a borrowed cow
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules about heirs of a borrower. They may use the cow for the rest of the borrowing period and are not liable if it dies. If they ate it thinking it was their father's, they pay only a low price for the meat. If their father left property with a lien, they must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If their father left them a borrowed cow, they may use it for the whole borrowing period. If it died, they are not liable for the accident. If they thought it was their father's and slaughtered and ate it, they pay for the meat at a cheap price. If their father left them property that carries a lien, they must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling about children who inherit a cow their father had borrowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heirs did not borrow the cow themselves, so they do not take on the borrower's liability for accidents. When they ate it by mistake, they pay only for what they benefited, at a low meat price. But if the father left property with a lien, the payment obligation goes with that property, so they must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Their father left them (as an inheritance)
The days of its borrowing period
The price of meat at a cheap rate
Property that carries a lien (land that guarantees payment)

phrases.english: Rava said:
If their father left them a borrowed cow,
they may use it
for the whole borrowing period.
If it died, they are not liable for its accident.
If they thought it was their father's
and they slaughtered it and ate it,
they pay the price of the meat at a cheap rate.
If their father left them property that carries a lien,
phrases.notes: This means land the father owned that guaranteed his debts, so the obligation goes with the land.

phrases.english: they are obligated to pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הִנִּיחַ לָהֶן אֲבִיהֶן פָּרָה שְׁאוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related ruling about borrowed cows, this time for the borrower's heirs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heirs may use the borrowed cow and are not liable for accidents. If they ate it by mistake, they pay a low meat price. If the father left property with a lien, they must pay.

steps.title: Two versions of where רבא's last line applies
steps.stepSummary: Some apply 'they must pay' to the first case (the cow died), and some apply it only to the last case (they ate it). The first version disagrees with רב פפא; the second agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach the last line on the first part, and some teach it on the last part. The one who teaches it on the first part would say it all the more so on the last part, and this disagrees with רב פפא. The one who teaches it on the last part, but not on the first part, matches רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports two versions of which case רבא's line about property with a lien refers to, and links each version to רב פפא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If heirs with liened property must pay even when the cow simply died, then the father's liability for accidents must have started when he borrowed it, which argues with רב פפא. If they pay only when they slaughtered and ate it, then liability for accidents starts only when the accident happens, which is exactly רב פפא's view from step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (there are two versions)
The first part of a ruling
The last part of a ruling
All the more so
It disagrees

steps.confusionAlert: Here רֵישָׁא means 'the cow died' and סֵיפָא means 'they slaughtered and ate it'. These are the two earlier cases in רבא's ruling, not the property-with-a-lien line itself.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether liability for accidents begins at the borrowing or at the accident decides whether רבא agrees with רב פפא. In one version he agrees, in the other he argues.

phrases.english: Some teach it on the first part,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the line 'they are obligated to pay'. The first part is when the cow died.

phrases.english: and some teach it on the last part.
phrases.notes: The last part is when they slaughtered and ate it.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it on the first part
would say it all the more so on the last part,
and this disagrees with Rav Pappa.
And the one who teaches it on the last part,
but not on the first part,
this matches Rav Pappa.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַרֵישָׁא, וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies which case of step 9 the last line refers to, and connects it to רב פפא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the version that applies the line to the first part, רבא argues with רב פפא. In the version that applies it only to the last part, he agrees with רב פפא.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש explain it like רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the earlier argument about the sister case. It understands why רבי יוחנן did not follow ריש לקיש, but asks why ריש לקיש did not follow רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבי יוחנן did not explain it like ריש לקיש, because he explains the משנה according to the רבנן. But what is ריש לקיש's reason for not explaining it like רבי יוחנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about one who violates his sister. It is setting up a question about ריש לקיש's choice, which is answered in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן explained the משנה as a case with no warning, which fits the רבנן. That is a good reason, since a plain משנה usually follows the רבנן. ריש לקיש instead said the משנה follows רבי מאיר, so the גמרא asks why he did not take רבי יוחנן's simpler path.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (granted), introducing one side before a question on the other
He sets it up (explains the case as)
The Sages (the majority view)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: It makes sense that Rabbi Yochanan
phrases.notes: We are back to the earlier argument about one who violates his sister: our משנה says he pays, but the משנה in מכות says he gets lashes.

phrases.english: did not explain it like Reish Lakish,
since he explains it according to the Rabbis.
But Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not explain it like Rabbi Yochanan?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא אָמַר כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the borrowed-cow discussion and returns to the earlier רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argument
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why ריש לקיש did not explain the משנה as a case with no warning, like רבי יוחנן

steps.title: No warning should not create a payment
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reasons that if a warned sinner is exempt from paying, an unwarned one should be exempt too. So רבי יוחנן's explanation does not work for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: since if they warned him he is exempt, when they did not warn him he is also exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש's reason for rejecting רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the רבנן, a warned sinner who gets lashes does not also pay. ריש לקיש holds that the missing warning should not change this: whatever exempts him from paying when warned also exempts him when not warned. So the משנה that makes him pay cannot be explained as a case with no warning, and it must follow רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (giving his reasoning)
They warned him (התראה before the sin)
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש holds that the exemption from paying does not depend on whether there was a warning. That is why he explains the משנה like רבי מאיר and not like רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
since if they had warned him, he is exempt,
phrases.notes: Exempt from the money payment, because he gets lashes instead.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ — נָמֵי פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: when they did not warn him, he is also exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If a warned sinner is exempt from paying, an unwarned one is exempt too, so the 'no warning' explanation cannot explain a משנה that obligates payment

steps.title: The two אמוראים follow their own wider reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are consistent. רב דימי reported a general dispute between them: does an unwarned sinner who deserves death or lashes have to pay money? רבי יוחנן says he pays, and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow their usual reasoning. When רב דימי came, he said: if someone sinned without warning in a sin that carries death, or in a sin that carries lashes, and the sin also involved money, רבי יוחנן says he must pay and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the argument about the sister case is part of a bigger, general argument between the same two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the argument seemed to be only about one case. Now רב דימי shows a general rule: רבי יוחנן always makes an unwarned sinner pay, and ריש לקיש always exempts him. So each one's view in the sister case fits his general opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning, which they hold in other places too
Sins that carry a death penalty
Sins that carry lashes
Here: done without a warning, so no physical punishment can be given
Another matter, meaning a money payment tied to the same act

steps.confusionAlert: Here שׁוֹגְגִין does not only mean 'by accident.' The next step shows it is about a sinner who was not warned. That is why he gets no death or lashes.

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning.
For when רב דימי came, he said:
Those who deserve death and acted unwittingly,
and those who deserve lashes and acted unwittingly, and there is another matter —
phrases.notes: The 'other matter' is a money payment that comes from the same act.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said: he is liable,
and ריש לקיש said: he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָזְדוּ לְטַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the positions explained in steps 11-12 come from a wider dispute between the same two אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an unwarned sinner whose sin deserves death or lashes and also involves money, רבי יוחנן says he pays and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a single case into a general rule about how physical punishment and money payment relate.

steps.title: The reasons behind each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן makes him pay because he was not warned, so no physical punishment applies. ריש לקיש exempts him: a warned sinner is exempt from paying, so an unwarned one is also exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, because they did not warn him. ריש לקיש says he is exempt, because if they had warned him he would be exempt, so when they did not warn him he is also exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא holds his view in רב דימי's dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the money is skipped only when a bigger punishment is actually given. With no warning, there is no bigger punishment, so he pays. For ריש לקיש, the act itself is the kind that cancels money, so the lack of warning does not bring the payment back.

keyTerms.meaning: They warned him, meaning the warning needed before a court can punish
Liable, obligated to pay
Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: no warning means no physical punishment, so he pays. ריש לקיש: if warned he would not pay, so unwarned he also does not pay.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said he is liable —
since they did not warn him.
ריש לקיש said he is exempt —
since if they had warned him, he would be exempt,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ — נָמֵי פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: when they did not warn him, he is also exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר חַיָּיב דְּהָא לָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the two rulings just reported by רב דימי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן ties the money exemption to an actual warning and punishment. ריש לקיש exempts even without a warning, since a warned sinner would be exempt.

steps.title: ריש לקיש begins a challenge from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש starts to challenge רבי יוחנן by quoting a פסוק about a pregnant woman hurt in a fight: if there is no deadly harm, the attacker must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן from the פסוק: 'And there is no harm, he shall surely be fined.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש opens a challenge against רבי יוחנן by quoting a פסוק. The full argument from the פסוק continues on the next amud, so this step is setting up the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק makes payment depend on 'no harm,' meaning the woman did not die. ריש לקיש is about to read this as proof that when death is involved there is no payment, even in a case like this one. That would go against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Harm or disaster; here, the woman's death
He shall surely be fined, meaning he must pay money

phrases.english: ריש לקיש raised an objection to רבי יוחנן:
"And there is no harm, he shall surely be fined,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both reasons are explained, ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's view from a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that an unwarned sinner who deserves death still pays money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires payment only when there is 'no harm' (no death). So when there is death, there is no payment, even though the case seems to have no warning. That goes against רבי יוחנן. The full argument continues on the next amud.
